reportTitle: Vampiric Remainder Lineage: The Crowned Blood
archiveStatus: Active and politically dispersed; individual court ties vary
executiveAssessment: The Crowned Blood descends from vampires who ruled domains, built courts, advised princes, and taught others to obey. Their titles survived in blood and memory. Their legal force did not.

Most Crowned read a room quickly. They notice who actually decides, who is being ignored, which promise keeps the peace, and where a frightened group needs direction. This can make them excellent negotiators and crisis leaders. It can also make them assume that recognizing power gives them the right to wield it.

Their chief internal enemy is the Crownless Regency: former court officers who place disposable rulers on the throne and govern from behind them. The dispute is simple. The Crowned say a ruler must carry the burden of rule. The Regency makes someone else carry the blame.
historicalRecord: Old records place the Crowned among domain rulers, court builders, hereditary governors, senior advisers, and elders. They did more than occupy thrones. They created offices, ceremonies, feeding rights, lines of succession, patronage debts, and the habits that made a court feel permanent.
They understood how a gathering became a court and how an emergency appointment became a lifelong title. They knew how to make a new order look ancient by the time anyone thought to question it.

Crowned histories call this stewardship. Their rivals call it domination taught to speak politely. Both accounts contain truth. Some Crowned courts prevented open slaughter and held unstable domains together. Others made violence harder to see by placing it behind ritual, etiquette, and inherited duty.
continuumExpression: An old title commands no one by itself. A court, state, spirit, machine intelligence, or Blacklight team may recognize a Crowned member's experience without recognizing the rank they claim.

What remains useful is their instinct for command, precedent, ceremony, and political memory. A capable Crowned can find the person everyone quietly depends upon, organize a failing evacuation, settle a disputed succession, or give a terrified group a plan they can follow.

What remains dangerous is the belief that skill at ruling proves a right to rule. In the present Continuum, authority must be earned through ability, agreement, leverage, or force. Only the first three can support lasting cooperation.
capabilityProfile: The lineage favors Grave Dominion and Blood Memory. These affinities support command, political pressure, inherited recollection, and the use of old court knowledge in present disputes.

Inherited Command only assists willing allies or acknowledged subordinates, and only after the Crowned member has already succeeded through Command or Negotiation. It strengthens an accepted plan. It does not force acceptance.

In a crisis, that distinction matters. A trusted Crowned leader can make an organized group act with frightening speed. An abusive leader can make a willing but dependent group carry out harm just as efficiently.
liabilityPressureProfile: The lineage Bane is Wounded Rank. Public refusal or public loss of an asserted title can provoke Hunger.
That reaction does not prove the Crowned member was owed obedience. It records the wound caused by refusal, not the justice of the order that was refused.

A Crowned member can prevent the increase by explicitly releasing the refusing person from obligation. Those who can do this without retaliation are generally safer allies than those who treat every refusal as rebellion.
Enemies know how to exploit this weakness. Staged humiliation, false demotion, contradictory orders, and public insubordination can push a Crowned member toward Hunger at exactly the wrong moment.

encounterTestimony.quote: He did not raise his voice. He named the exits, put three people on the wounded, and everyone moved. Ten minutes later he called it his court.
encounterTestimony.attribution: Blacklight field medic, evacuation of the Harrow Street shelter
encounterTestimony.custody: Post-operation voice statement, cross-checked against body-camera footage
encounterTestimony.context: The footage confirms the evacuation orders and the later use of the word court. It does not establish whether the speaker intended a formal claim.

encounterTestimony.quote: The prince changed twice. The same woman kept the keys, the feeding ledgers, and the emergency seal. We had been arguing with the wrong ruler.
encounterTestimony.attribution: Former clerk of an unnamed river-domain court
encounterTestimony.custody: Protected interview; identity withheld because the witness remains inside the court's feeding territory
encounterTestimony.context: The account matches several succession records but the alleged regent has not been directly interviewed.

internalAdversaryAssessment.name: The Crownless Regency
internalAdversaryAssessment.classification: Puppet sovereigns and dispossessed court officers
description: Former seneschals, regents, hereditary advisers, and dethroned elders who concluded that visible rulers are liabilities. They govern through replaceable princes, enthralled boards, forged succession records, and crises designed to prove that every domain requires their hidden hand.

The Regency is not made dangerous by incompetence. Its members are often excellent administrators. They are dangerous because they place the risk of rule on a public figure while keeping the real decisions elsewhere.
operatingMethod: They undermine legitimate authority, install dependent figureheads, and preserve emergency powers long after the emergency has passed.

They favor succession disputes, forged genealogies, controlled feeding access, enthralled advisers, selective court records, manufactured crises, and the quiet removal of rulers who learn to act without them.
personalConflict: The Crowned Blood sees rulership as a burden that must be justified. The Regency sees rulers as masks worn by whoever controls the room behind the throne.
For the Crowned, the Regency represents the ugliest possible answer to their own inheritance: keep the command, avoid the danger, and let someone else be hated for it.
assessment: Suspect Regency influence when rulers change but the same advisers, creditors, heralds, feeding officers, and emergency rules remain in place. Experienced staff are not proof by themselves. The question is whether the people giving the real orders can be named, challenged, and removed.

The Regency recruits Crowned vampires who are tired of assassination, public refusal, or court humiliation. It offers them power without exposure. In practice, it moves the cost of Wounded Rank onto a disposable prince and everyone beneath them.
unresolvedLinks: It is not known whether the Crownless Regency is one organization, several related courts, or a method repeatedly rediscovered by dispossessed officers.
Its reach inside current emergency governments and corporate boards remains unconfirmed.

blacklightAssessment: Judge a Crowned vampire by what happens when someone says no. A member who states the limits of a role, accepts review, releases unwilling followers, and answers for their orders can be a valuable ally.
Trace who gives orders, who controls feeding and resources, who can make exceptions, and who remains after rulers change. The person on the throne may not be the person in command.
Do not call every Crowned vampire a tyrant. That drives useful allies toward courts that promise protection and helps the Regency argue that public responsibility is merely a way to identify targets.
Do not make the opposite mistake either. Courtesy, competence, old knowledge, and sincere duty do not make coercion acceptable.

recognitionIndicators: Inherited titles used where no one has agreed to honor them.
Detailed knowledge of precedence, succession, ceremony, and the people whose private approval controls a public office.
A habit of turning a crisis into named roles, duties, and witnessed orders.
Visible anger, distress, or Hunger after public refusal or demotion.
Rulers change while advisers, creditors, feeding officers, and emergency powers remain untouched.
negotiationConsiderations: State exactly what role is being recognized and where that role ends.
Say whether the Crowned member is advising, coordinating, commanding by consent, or claiming sovereign power.
Provide a clear way to revise or end an obligation.
Do not offer ceremonial deference until its meaning has been translated.
Avoid needless public humiliation. This reduces risk; it does not concede obedience.
evidenceHandling: Preserve orders, exceptions, succession records, emergency declarations, advisory minutes, feeding allocations, and the names of people who remained powerful across several rulers.
Separate the public ruler's choices from conditions imposed by hidden advisers.
Record whether followers were willing, formally bound, coerced, dependent, enthralled, or simply assumed to obey.
Treat ceremonial wording as possible evidence until its meaning is known.
escalationThresholds: A Crowned actor uses force, feeding control, domination, or deprivation to turn a disputed claim into obedience.
An adviser gives binding orders while a public ruler carries the blame.
Emergency powers continue after the emergency with no clear way to end them.
Public refusal is answered with retaliation instead of release, review, or negotiation.
prohibitedAssumptions: Inherited rank does not create present authority.
Not every Crowned vampire wants to rule.
Effective cooperation does not prove enthrallment.
The visible ruler may not be the real decision-maker.
Pain caused by refusal does not make the refused order rightful.
withdrawalConditions: The team cannot identify who actually gives the orders.
A ceremony would create an obligation whose limits cannot be explained.
A Crowned liaison refuses any right of release, appeal, or refusal while retaining the power to punish.
The negotiation is being used to install or legitimize a Regency puppet.

unresolvedIntelligence: It remains unclear whether Wounded Rank is one shared supernatural inheritance or several court habits reinforced over centuries.
The number of Blood Courts that still honor Crowned titles is unknown. Some recognize only specific offices; others reject the old claims entirely.
No reliable count separates accountable Crowned leaders from those using Crownless Regency methods.
Court histories disagree on where the first Regency began. The method may have arisen more than once.
Inherited Command has not been sufficiently tested with synthetic persons, distributed minds, or groups that recognize roles without recognizing a single ruler.

gift.name: Inherited Command
gift.effect: Once per scene after succeeding on Presence + Command or Presence + Negotiation, choose up to Archetype Rating willing allies or acknowledged subordinates within 10 meters. Until the end of your next turn, each gains one die on actions directly carrying out the plan or order you just stated.

bane.name: Wounded Rank
bane.effect: The first time each scene a person publicly refuses an order you directly issued or strips you of an asserted title, gain 1 Hunger. Prevent this increase by explicitly releasing that person from obligation before the end of your next turn.
